_comment: Every capability the listing claims, bound to the parity rows that have to
read `done` in the Android column of shared/docs/parity.md before that claim
may be published. Read by check_fidelity.py.
This file exists because of the first of the two reasons Compliance blocked
the original listing copy, and it is the reason that needed no legal reading
at all: a first-release listing whose headline feature is absent from the APK
is a misrepresentation in the store. That was true of `Buy bitcoin` in the
first draft. It is equally true of on-chain send, Lightning, the recovery
phrase walkthrough and the Academy in the replacement draft — none of which
exist in the Android build today either. The rule is the same rule; it just
has to be applied to every claim rather than to the one that was noticed.
`feature` matches column 1 of a parity.md row exactly.
One claim was deleted from this file rather than gated: `lightning-auto-
connection`, the sentence "Smaller amounts can open a Lightning connection
for you automatically ...". It was the only claim here that a finished port
would not have made true, because the capability is delivered by the purchase
service and not by the wallet: connectOpenChannel has one call site and it is
commented out (DeviceViewController.swift:197), so the app never opens a
channel itself. Ruben deleted it permanently on 2026-09-13 (BIT-37 card
f7f8ac6f, `delete-permanently`). It does not come back when the Lightning
parity rows go green, and check_listing.py now carries a hard rule so an edit
cannot reintroduce it quietly — that rule, not this note, is the guard.

claims.quote: The wallet is non-custodial ... bittr never takes custody of it
claims.note: True by construction, not by feature: the seed is generated on device and held in the platform keystore, and Bittr is not a counterparty to the wallet (perimeter P9). Nothing to gate — recorded here so the set of claims is complete rather than only the gated ones.

claims.quote: the app walks you through writing down your recovery phrase before you put anything into it
claims.note: Phase 4 stage 2. Today the Android build reaches SignupStartScreen and its two buttons are backed by StubWalletService — there is no mnemonic screen to walk anyone through.

claims.quote: Send and receive on the Bitcoin network
or over Lightning for payments that settle in seconds
The built-in Academy explains custody, recovery phrases, addresses, Lightning ...
claims.note: Phase 4 stage 10 — later in the plan than Buy at stage 8.

claims.quote: bittr is made by Bittr AG, a company registered in Ibach, Schwyz, Switzerland
claims.note: A fact about the company, not a feature of the binary. Verified against the site footer (perimeter E1).
